title: Andrew’s Roast Chicken

items.raw: ½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 pound carrots or small potatoes, cut into chunks (optional)

steps.text: Pat the chicken very dry inside and out. Season all over with the salt and pepper; if there is time, refrigerate uncovered overnight for crisper skin.
Set it to 425°F. Let the chicken sit out 30 minutes while it heats.
Rub the butter over the skin. Put the lemon halves, garlic, and thyme inside the cavity and tie the legs together.
Toss the vegetables with the oil and a pinch of salt and spread them in a roasting pan or skillet. Set the chicken on top, breast side up.
Roast 60 to 75 minutes, until the skin is golden, the juices run clear, and the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F.
Rest 15 minutes, then carve. Squeeze the roasted lemon over the pan juices and spoon them over the meat.

notes.label: Dry skin is crisp skin
notes.text: the overnight uncovered rest in the refrigerator makes the biggest difference.

notes.label: Simple pan sauce
notes.text: set the pan over medium heat, add ½ cup stock or white wine, scrape up the browned bits, and swirl in a tablespoon of butter.

notes.label: Spatchcocked
notes.text: cut out the backbone, flatten the bird, and roast at 450°F for about 45 minutes.

openQuestion: This is a best guess — a classic butter-and-lemon roast chicken. What makes Andrew’s distinct: the seasoning, a spatchcock, a particular pan or vegetables underneath, a gravy? And when does he make it?
